## What it is

**What it is:** a bridge between a Zigbee radio network and MQTT. It talks to a Zigbee coordinator (adapter), pairs sensors, lights, plugs and switches from many vendors, and publishes their state to an MQTT broker, so Home Assistant, Node-RED or any MQTT client can use them without a vendor hub. Upstream: "Zigbee to MQTT bridge, get rid of your proprietary Zigbee bridges" (https://www.zigbee2mqtt.io). In OneMind it is part of the greenhouse and family profiles with Home Assistant and Mosquitto (research `13-apps-market-plugins.md`, brief 30 B10).

**Icon:** `icon.svg` is a neutral generated icon (initials), not the upstream logo.

## How it is packaged

- **Image:** the upstream image `ghcr.io/koenkk/zigbee2mqtt`, built by upstream CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) and named in the [Docker install guide](https://www.zigbee2mqtt.io/guide/installation/02_docker.html). The tag is the release, pinned by the multi-arch index digest; the index also carries arm/v6, arm/v7, riscv64 and 386, which OneMind does not declare.
- **Non-root:** the image has no `USER` and runs as root by default. Upstream documents running it as UID/GID 1000 (Docker guide, "Rootless container"; compose `user: 1000:1000`). The pod sets `runAsNonRoot`, UID/GID 1000 and `fsGroup: 1000` for the data volume, plus `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false`, all Linux capabilities dropped, `RuntimeDefault` seccomp and no service-account token.
- **State:** one PVC `zigbee2mqtt-data` (1 Gi, the k3s default `local-path` class) on `/app/data`: `configuration.yaml`, the Zigbee network database, the coordinator backup and logs. Back it up: losing it means re-pairing every device. One replica with the `Recreate` strategy, so two pods never drive the coordinator at once.
- **Network:** Service `zigbee2mqtt`, port 8080 (onboarding page, then the frontend over HTTP and WebSocket).
- **Health:** startup, readiness and liveness probes on `GET /`, which the onboarding server and the frontend both answer.

## No USB coordinator in v0

A Zigbee2MQTT install needs a Zigbee coordinator. Upstream's usual setup passes a USB adapter into the container (`--device=/dev/serial/by-id/...` and `-v /run/udev:/run/udev:ro`). **This v0 package has no device access:** it mounts no host device and no `/run/udev`, and it runs unprivileged, so a USB stick plugged into the box cannot be used yet. Device passthrough needs a OneMind device-access design (node pinning, a device plugin or a host-path exception), which is a later contract change.

What works today:

- **A network (Ethernet or Wi-Fi) coordinator.** Upstream supports adapters reached over TCP, for example `serial.port: tcp://<adapter-host>:<port>` ([Connect to a remote adapter](https://www.zigbee2mqtt.io/advanced/remote-adapter/connect_to_a_remote_adapter.html)). The pod needs only network access to the adapter.
- **Without any adapter** the onboarding page runs, and after a submitted configuration fails to start, upstream runs the onboarding again on the next start (getting-started guide, "Onboarding"). Zigbee2MQTT does not bridge any device until a coordinator is reachable.

## First run

From the upstream getting-started guide, https://www.zigbee2mqtt.io/guide/getting-started/#onboarding:

1. Have an MQTT broker reachable from the cluster, for example the OneMind Mosquitto app (its Service in namespace `app-mosquitto`), and a network Zigbee coordinator.
2. Open the app's web UI (port 8080) from the OneMind dashboard. With no `configuration.yaml` yet, Zigbee2MQTT shows its **onboarding** page.
3. Enter the adapter: `tcp://<adapter-host>:<port>` and the adapter type (`zstack`, `ember`, `deconz`, `zigate` or `zboss`; see https://www.zigbee2mqtt.io/guide/adapters/). Serial discovery finds nothing here because the pod has no devices.
4. Enter the MQTT server (`mqtt://<broker-service>.<namespace>.svc:1883`) and its user and password if the broker requires them.
5. Keep the frontend enabled, and set a frontend `auth_token` (https://www.zigbee2mqtt.io/guide/configuration/frontend.html): the frontend has no login by default, and anyone who reaches port 8080 can control your devices.
6. Submit. Zigbee2MQTT writes `/app/data/configuration.yaml` and starts. Pair devices with **Permit join** in the frontend (https://www.zigbee2mqtt.io/guide/usage/pairing_devices.html).

To run the onboarding again later, set the environment variable `Z2M_ONBOARD_FORCE_RUN=1` on the container (same upstream section).

## Sizing

Upstream publishes no sizing guidance. Measured in the OneMind smoke test (2026-11-12, k3s v1.37.2+k3s1, arm64): 33 Mi and 1m CPU while the onboarding page waits, with no adapter and no devices. A running bridge grows with the number of devices, so the request (50m / 128 Mi) and limit (1 CPU / 512 Mi) leave headroom, and the Market lists `minMemoryMb: 256`. Raise the limit for a large network if the pod is OOM-killed.

## Known limits in this package

- **No USB adapter** (above). The `TZ` variable from the upstream examples is not set, so logs use UTC.
- **The onboarding page is unauthenticated.** Until the first configuration is submitted, anyone who can reach port 8080 can configure the app or upload a data archive. The Service is cluster-internal (`ClusterIP`); keep it that way until onboarding is done.
- **GPL-3.0:** OneMind ships the upstream image unchanged as a separate program. The corresponding source is upstream's tag `2.14.3`.
